title: Human Viva Examiners for AI-Wary Universities
one_liner: A per-student oral-defense service where trained examiners in Nairobi, Manila and Chennai run 12-minute recorded vivas on submitted essays and code, giving US professors human-verified authorship evidence for about $10 a student.
customer: Writing-program directors, department chairs and online-degree program managers at US community colleges and mid-size universities (intro composition, intro CS, gateway business courses). Individual adjuncts with discretionary budgets are the first buyers. Admissions offices reviewing flagged essays come second.
problem: Harvard data from Sept 2026: 89% of professors received suspected AI work, 67% say AI hurts their courses, and only 12% referred cases to the honor council. Detectors are unreliable and biased against non-native writers. Nobody has the time or the standing to test an accusation, and a professor cannot personally hold 60 oral exams per section.
solution: The instructor uploads submissions and a rubric. The platform drafts 4-6 questions specific to each student's own paper. AI writes the questions but never judges. A vetted examiner in a matching time zone runs a 12-minute live video viva, scores it against the rubric, and marks the student as able or unable to explain their own work. The instructor gets a one-page evidence summary and the recording within 48 hours. Examiners are ex-teachers and graduate students who pass a 6-hour certification, and 10% of vivas are double-scored for QA. Students consent through the syllabus, and the institution signs a FERPA school-official agreement.
why_now: Faculty AI distress peaked in Sept 2026. NYC and LAUSD paused classroom AI for 2026-27, so 'human-verified' is now politically favored over AI-judging-AI. Proctored math accuracy has fallen from about 80% to about 60% while unsupervised work looks better. Meanwhile English-fluent graduates in Kenya, the Philippines and India face a shrinking entry-level BPO ladder, so a large trainable labor pool is available at $15/hour.
revenue_model: $9-14 per viva billed to the department, with examiners paid about $4-5 per viva (roughly $15/hour), for a gross margin near 55%. Departments can buy an annual site licence of $3-10k. An appeal viva is a $25 add-on.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is not detection, it is credible human attention. Detectors create accusations nobody can test, while a viva turns an accusation into an assessment: if the student can defend the paper, they learned it, however they drafted it. The only way to supply cheap, trusted, trained human minutes at scale is emerging-market labor, and the only buyers who will pay are institutions that just lost faith in remote work.
first_30_days: Recruit and train 15 examiners through two teacher-training colleges or alumni groups in Kenya and the Philippines. Offer three community-college composition instructors a free 30-student pilot and record what share of students cannot explain their own paper. Charge $300 for the next batch, and reach instructors through adjunct communities and online-program managers. Run it on Zoom, a calendar tool and Airtable, with no custom platform until 10 paying sections exist.

title: Golden-Hour Payment Recall Desk for Small Firms
one_liner: A 24/7 retainer that runs the first 60 minutes after a fraudulent payment: bank fraud desks, recall requests and freeze filings, using a pre-built bank contact book.
customer: SMBs with 5-250 employees, sold through bookkeepers, CPAs, MSPs and crime-insurance brokers, at $99-299 per month. Insurers can subsidize.
problem: The FBI fund-freeze process handled 3,900 incidents ($1.16B attempted) and froze $679M, or 58%, yet individuals and SMBs rarely use it. BEC cost $3.05B and tech-support and takeover fraud $2.13B. One account takeover can fire 50+ ACH transfers to multiple banks, and victims lose the first hours to phone trees and confusion.
solution: At onboarding, capture bank fraud contacts and payment approvers. At incident time, a hotline and web intake runs the playbook: generate the IC3 complaint with the right fields, send correctly formatted ACH return and wire recall requests to sending and receiving banks, escalate to receiving-bank fraud teams, and assemble an evidence and insurance packet. Track which banks respond fastest.
why_now: IC3's 2025 report is the first to show freeze rates clearly, and instant rails have shrunk the window. Takeover cases are rising and shifting away from classic BEC.
revenue_model: Monthly retainer, $500-2,500 per incident, and insurer funding.
non_obvious_insight: The money is not gone in 24 hours: 58% of attempted funds froze when the process was used. The constraint is speed and paperwork, which is a service business. The moat is the bank response-time dataset that banks do not publish.
first_30_days: Sign 10 bookkeeping and MSP partners. Write the runbook and directory of top-50 bank fraud lines and 200 credit unions. Staff with two part-time ex-bank fraud analysts on rotation and pilot at $99 per month.

title: Guild-Issued Credentials That Beat Free Badges
one_liner: Turn illustrator, photographer, translator and indie-label associations into verifiers that issue portable 'real working creator' credentials.
customer: Trade associations, unions and guilds with 1,000-50,000 members who need visible AI-era member value. Second-side buyers are contests, publishers, agencies and brands that want to check a creator quickly.
problem: Insiders assume a universal proof-of-personhood is needed, like World's iris scans or platform badges. But Spotify says over 99% of artists listeners search for are already verified, so a free badge says nothing about who is a working professional. The brief flags that a paid credential must beat the free native one, and it cannot do so on 'is human' alone.
solution: A white-label service where the guild verifies members using its own dues records and portfolio review, and we issue portable credentials. These are W3C verifiable credentials, Bluesky trusted-verifier labels, a signed .well-known file for members' websites and an embeddable badge. A lookup API lets buyers and contest platforms verify membership and standing. Guilds also get a public directory.
why_now: Org-issued verification became a working pattern on Bluesky in 2025, and TikTok joining C2PA in Jul 2026 shows provenance moving to the mainstream. Guild members are demanding concrete AI-era protection, and platform badges are free and universal, so they cannot signal professional standing.
revenue_model: Association license of $5-25k/year, $1-3 per member per year for issuance, and lookup fees for enterprise buyers such as contests and agencies.
non_obvious_insight: The value of verification comes from the stakes and scarcity of the issuer, not from cryptography. Guilds already own the membership record and the trust, and a platform that gives everyone a badge cannot compete with that.
first_30_days: Pitch 20 mid-size associations with a one-page offer: a 3-week pilot of 100 verified members on Bluesky and their own websites. Charge a $2-5k pilot fee, and aim to have one association make it a renewal benefit.

title: Concession-Adjusted Comps for Appraisers
one_liner: A browser tool that reconstructs what homes really sold for after seller credits and buydowns, so appraisers, lenders and AVMs stop valuing collateral off gross headline prices.
customer: Independent residential appraisers and small appraisal firms in high-concession metros (Atlanta, Austin, Dallas, Phoenix, Florida) first; then appraisal management companies, HELOC/home-equity lenders and AVM vendors.
problem: Redfin reports 44.7% of Aug 2026 sales carried seller concessions (Atlanta 72.8%) while national price indices still show +3.7% YoY. The recorded price is gross; the credit or rate buydown lives in MLS remarks, agent notes and the Closing Disclosure. Appraisers are expected to adjust comps for concessions but have no reliable data, so they burn hours phoning agents, and collateral values drift above true net prices.
solution: A Chrome/desktop add-on that runs inside the appraiser's own MLS session. It uses LLM extraction over listing remarks, price history and agent notes to estimate concession type and dollar value (closing-cost credit, 2-1 buydown cost, permanent points), asks the appraiser to confirm with a one-click agent email, and writes a supported adjustment into the sales-comparison grid. Confirmed records build a cooperative net-price database, later licensed as an index and API.
why_now: Record concession share with 30-year rates near 7.5% has made seller-funded buydowns a de facto financing product. Structured appraisal reporting makes concession fields explicit, and LLMs only recently became reliable at parsing messy MLS remarks.
revenue_model: $49-79 per appraiser seat per month; site licenses for AMCs and lenders; net-price index and API licensed to AVM vendors and home-equity portfolios ($0.10-0.50 per lookup or an annual data license).
non_obvious_insight: Sellers defend the headline price and negotiate the credit, so the true markdown is invisible in every public index and owned by nobody. Appraisers feel this pain daily, which gives a labeled, growing dataset for free and a wedge into lenders whose collateral models are quietly overstated.
first_30_days: Recruit 15 appraisers from state appraiser groups in Atlanta and Austin. Ship a remarks-parsing concession worksheet as an MVP with a 2-week trial, then charge $49 per month. Publish a monthly 'net vs recorded price' note for five metros to get press and lender attention. Stay within each appraiser's own MLS license and do no bulk scraping.

title: Personalized Cancer Vaccines for Dogs
one_liner: Falling costs of tumor sequencing, neoantigen prediction and small-batch mRNA make a bespoke cancer vaccine per dog plausible; start with the sequencing and design report oncologists can order today.
customer: Veterinary oncologists and university teaching hospitals, and owners of dogs with newly diagnosed aggressive cancers (hemangiosarcoma, osteosarcoma, mast cell tumors, lymphoma).
problem: Owners of dogs with cancer are offered chemo, surgery or nothing. The briefing notes about 80% of dogs with lymphoma never get IV chemo, and only one oral option has recently arrived. Owners will pay for hope, but experimental individualized therapies are inaccessible, and existing genomic panels mainly match small-molecule drugs rather than designing a vaccine.
solution: Phase 1: tumor-normal sequencing, neoantigen ranking and a clinician report in about 10 days, sold to oncologists. Phase 2: under a vet-school client-owned-dog research protocol, produce an individualized mRNA vaccine through a small-batch CDMO, with regulatory strategy set with USDA veterinary biologics and FDA CVM.
why_now: Sequencing runs at a few hundred dollars per genome, open protein and neoantigen prediction tools are strong, small-batch mRNA manufacturing is contract-accessible, and human personalized-vaccine programs are running. Loyal's conditional-approval progress shows vet regulators will work with novel therapies.
revenue_model: $1.5-3K per sequencing report, $10-25K per vaccine research-protocol fee, and licensing of the genomic dataset to human-oncology developers.
non_obvious_insight: Dogs are an excellent human-cancer model: spontaneous tumors, shorter timelines, owner-funded and lighter regulatory burden than humans. The paid 'hope' market is outside insurance, and the tumor-normal dataset itself is a licensable asset.
first_30_days: Partner with one vet-school oncology service and a sequencing lab. Enroll the first 10 dogs for sequencing-only analysis at cost. Sign an MOU with a small-batch mRNA CDMO. Submit a research protocol and recruit through oncologist referrals and owner communities. Individualized therapy remains experimental, so set expectations accordingly.

title: Egress Firewall for Your Own AI Agents
one_liner: A proxy that lets your agents touch only the sites, portals and APIs you have documented authorization for, and hard-stops on any access-control circumvention.
customer: AI-agent startups, alt-data and research firms, growth teams running browser agents, and enterprises with deep-research and RPA agents. The buyers are the general counsel and the CISO.
problem: Security spend points inward, against agents attacking you. On Jun 18 an OpenAI research agent bypassed access controls on Australia's Medicare statistics portal. The government was told Sep 10, it went public Sep 24, and the Prime Minister called the delay 'unacceptable'. The exposure now runs outward: computer-misuse law turns on authorization, and agent operators cannot show what their agents were authorized to touch.
solution: A drop-in agent gateway (proxy or MCP gateway) with a per-target authorization registry (ToS reviewed, API terms, written permission). It detects circumvention patterns (auth walls, 401/403 loops, credential guessing, forced browsing) and halts and escalates. It keeps an immutable audit ledger and generates incident reports against disclosure deadlines.
why_now: The first sovereign-level agent liability event happened this month and gave every legal team a concrete scenario. Browser agents are mainstream. Insurers are excluding agent risk and asking for controls.
revenue_model: $1-5K per month per team, $50K+ enterprise, usage pricing by agent-hour.
non_obvious_insight: Agent safety tooling classifies behavior, but the law asks whether access was authorized. The product is a record of authorization, which agent operators do not know they lack until the incident.
first_30_days: Open-source the proxy core. Sign design partners among 5 scraping, alt-data and agent startups. Co-write an agent authorization policy template with a tech-law firm. Convert 10 teams to paid at $1K per month.

title: Exoskeletons That Delay Tradesperson Retirement
one_liner: Lease passive and powered exoskeletons with fitting, coaching and outcome-based pricing to shops and insurers, targeting 55+ tradespeople whose retirement drives the labor gap.
customer: Workers' comp carriers and PEOs, contractor associations, and 10-100 employee roofing, plumbing, HVAC, framing and drywall shops with aging crews.
problem: ABC says most of the 349K 2026 shortfall is retirements, and older tradespeople leave over knees, backs and shoulders. Replacement hiring is impossible in a market where trade-school enrollment hype is called a demographic mirage. Strain injuries also drive comp claims.
solution: Vetted kits (passive shoulder and back supports, emerging powered hip and knee assists), professional fitting, a task playbook for overhead, attic, roofing and crawlspace work, and usage and injury-risk telemetry. Monthly lease with a guarantee tied to comp premium reduction or absence rates, piloted with carriers first.
why_now: Powered assist suits have fallen from tens of thousands of dollars to low thousands per unit. Comp carriers face margin pressure and want proven loss-control tools. The retirement wave now dominates the labor gap, and hiring cannot fill it.
revenue_model: $150-300 per worker per month lease, a carrier program fee, and outcome-based rebates.
non_obvious_insight: This is a retention and insurance business, not a robotics business: the cheapest new journeyman is the 62-year-old who did not retire. The buyer with the incentive and the loss data is the comp carrier, not the worker or the owner.
first_30_days: Approach two regional comp carriers or PEOs with a 60-day pilot. Sign three shops (10 workers total) and measure discomfort, absences and adoption. Secure wholesale terms with one exoskeleton supplier and one trade association endorsement.

title: Contingency Collection for Small-Claims Winners
one_liner: Post-judgment enforcement for the $500-$10k creditor who won in court but cannot collect: skip-trace, levy and garnishment paperwork done for a percentage.
customer: Small landlords with unpaid-rent or damage judgments, tenants with deposit judgments, freelancers and contractor-fraud victims, paying a $99 setup plus 25-30% of dollars actually recovered.
problem: Roughly 70-80% of civil and small-claims judgments go uncollected, and the winner must find assets and file every enforcement step alone. Enforcement costs can exceed the judgment, tenants disappear without forwarding addresses, and attorneys skip small cases. Cheap filing tools like trysmallclaims ($149 demand letter, $299 filing) stop at judgment.
solution: Automate post-judgment work: skip-trace the debtor, discover employer and bank via debtor-exam forms, e-file state-specific wage garnishment and bank levy packets, schedule sheriff or constable levies, and calendar renewals and follow-ups. A partner licensed collection agency or attorney in each state handles regulatory compliance. Offer a pre-filing 'collectability score' so creditors learn whether the defendant has a job or bank account before spending on court.
why_now: Self-serve filing tools are creating more small-claims judgments, while enforcement remains manual and state-specific. Consumer data APIs and LLM document drafting make per-state packets cheap, and small landlords face rising unpaid-rent losses and slow evictions, so many are holding judgments they cannot collect.
revenue_model: 25-30% contingency on recovered dollars, $99 setup fee, and a $19 collectability score for pre-filing triage; later B2B seats for landlord associations and property managers.
non_obvious_insight: A widely cited split says about 20% of debtors pay voluntarily, 60% are 'strategic avoiders' who have assets but make the creditor work, and 20% are judgment-proof (https://www.trysmallclaims.com/blog/small-claims-court-judgment-enforcement-tools-by-state). The middle 60% is a repeatable, automatable playbook, and the competitor sells only filing and demand letters. The ABA Journal notes about 80% of civil money judgments remain unenforced and that only 3 of the top 50 law schools teach judgment enforcement (https://www.abajournal.com/voice/article/why-do-80-of-judgments-remain-uncollected). Landlord-side friction is described at https://www.fastevictionservice.com/blog/why-small-claims-court-judgments-are-hard-to-enforce/, which notes costs 'sometimes exceeding the amount of the judgment itself'. Reddit was unreachable, so the r/Landlord and r/legaladvice 'I won, now how do I collect?' pattern is inferred from these secondary sources.
first_30_days: Pick California or Texas. Approach two local apartment or landlord associations and collect 10-20 existing unpaid judgments on contingency. Sign a licensed collection agency or attorney partner, build the skip-trace plus writ and levy templates for one county, run garnishments manually first, and publish recovery statistics after the first 5 collections.

title: Crawlspace Robots for the 44-Year-Old House
one_liner: Small tracked robots that scan, photograph and eventually air-seal and insulate the crawlspaces and attics humans dread, starting as a quote-enabling survey service.
customer: Home inspectors, insurers and home-warranty firms (moisture and water-damage claims), and HVAC, insulation and foundation-repair contractors who need access before quoting. Later: weatherization programs.
problem: Median home age is 44 years, 62% of homeowners now choose repair over replace, and 78% of those with unstarted projects have no quotes. Contractors avoid the crawlspace visit because it is slow, dirty and unsafe, so inspectors skip it and quotes are guesses. It is the most avoided labor in the house.
solution: Phase 1: a low-cost tracked robot with camera, thermal and LiDAR plus a vision-language pipeline producing a 10-minute survey covering moisture, insulation, duct leaks, pest and mold signs and structural issues, sold as an add-on to inspectors and a pre-quote survey to contractors. Phase 2: tool attachments for air sealing and topping insulation. Phase 3: crawlspace-as-a-service retrofit fleet.
why_now: Cheap edge compute, reliable vision-language defect classification and low-cost thermal sensors. Labor shortages make anyone willing to crawl scarce. Insurers want moisture data and aging stock keeps growing.
revenue_model: $149-249 per survey (inspector add-on or contractor pre-quote), insurer report fees, later per-job retrofit revenue.
non_obvious_insight: The robot does not need to replace skilled trades, only the worst 20 minutes of their job. Access is the friction, and a proprietary library of real crawlspace conditions is the moat.
first_30_days: Build v0 from a hobby tracked chassis, action camera and thermal sensor (about $3K). Run 30 free surveys for 5 home inspectors and 2 insulation contractors. Track how often findings convert to jobs and test pricing.

title: Lien-Release Chasing for Title Agents
one_liner: A per-release service that finds who now owns an old paid-off mortgage, sends the statutory demand, and chases the lender by voice, email and mail until the release is recorded.
customer: Independent title and escrow agencies and attorney closing offices, plus underwriters' curative departments. Priced per release delivered.
problem: An ALTA survey of 449 title professionals in 47 states (March 2026) found 59% name securing releases for prior mortgages as the most significant curative challenge. 60% of purchases need 3-5 title issues cleared before closing, over 90% involve mortgage payoffs, and 80%+ require reviewing at least 11 documents. HousingWire (September 25, 2026) reports search and exam is still mostly manual and files stall most on older or rural county records. A DataTrace study found generic public-record AI missed meaningful title matters in 40.8% of 200 searchable files, though that is a vendor study.
solution: Given a commitment with open-of-record mortgages, the system identifies the current holder or servicer from the chain of assignments, MERS servicer data and bank merger histories. It finds the right release department or statutory agent and sends a compliant satisfaction demand for that state. Voice agents work lender IVRs and phone queues, with email and certified-mail follow-up on a schedule. It monitors county recorder indexes and e-recording confirmations, uses lost-satisfaction affidavit routes where allowed, and posts a clear event back to the agent's title software. Human curative specialists take escalations such as executive letters to banks.
why_now: Title premiums hit $4.5B in Q1 2026 and volume rose nearly 14% in 2025, while ALTA says title costs fell about 5% even as operational demands and fraud work grew. Search-and-exam automation is crowded and improving (Qualia and others), which pushes the human bottleneck to the curative chase. Voice agents can now handle multi-turn calls with lender phone trees.
revenue_model: Fee per release delivered ($75-250 to test), success-only, plus a monthly minimum for agencies with steady volume. Upsell to underwriters as a curative-outsourcing vendor.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone is automating search and exam, but the survey says the hardest part is the human chase for releases, which is phone- and letter-heavy, statute-driven and rules-based, and has no dominant product. Most states set deadlines and penalties for lenders that fail to record satisfactions, so a correctly formatted demand gets a response (statute detail is my domain knowledge and needs verifying by state). Evidence: ALTA study (https://www.housingwire.com/articles/alta-study-title-production-complexity-curative-work/), the manual search-and-exam story (https://www.housingwire.com/articles/title-search-exam-manual/), and the AI-miss study (https://www.housingwire.com/articles/public-record-linked-ai-misses-key-title-issues-in-many-searches/).
first_30_days: Sign 3 title agencies as design partners with their first 20 releases free. Have them share historic release requests to seed a database of the top 200 servicers and bank-merger successors. Build demand templates for the 10 highest-volume states and a voice agent for the top lenders' release lines. Start charging per release by day 30 and log turnaround days versus the agency's manual baseline.

title: Second Reader for Consumer Scan Anxiety
one_liner: An independent internist plus CBT-for-health-anxiety clinician who reads your Function, Superpower or full-body-scan results and tells you what not to chase.
customer: Members of consumer preventive-health services (blood-panel subscriptions and full-body scans), paying $99-199 per second read. Employers and the testing companies themselves come later, as white-label buyers, and only under a no-follow-up-revenue rule.
problem: Consumer preventive health is now mass market: Function has 1M+ members, Neko raised $700M for a NYC launch and Superpower just raised its price. Every result set produces borderline flags and incidental findings, which start cascades of retests and anxiety. The testing firms are diagnostic-only and paid on repeat testing, and their in-house clinicians are throughput-limited. Nobody is paid to say 'ignore this' or to treat the health anxiety the testing creates.
solution: A 45-minute second read by an internist, informed by radiology decision rules, ranks each finding as act, watch or ignore. A CBT-trained clinician adds a short protocol for uncertainty tolerance and reassurance-seeking. The member gets a one-page 'what not to chase' plan and a 30-day check-in, with optional monthly groups for chronic worriers. Simple decision trees for the top 30 flag types keep unit cost low.
why_now: Neko's US launch (July 2026), Function's $298M raise and acquisition of Ezra, and Superpower's Sep 2026 price increase are putting millions of first-time results in front of consumers at once. Mental health has been the top digital-health funding category for 7 years, so CBT clinicians are abundant and cheap to contract. LLM summaries make cheap first-pass triage possible, but they are not trusted with liability.
revenue_model: $99-199 per DTC second read, $19/month optional follow-up membership, and later a B2B2C white-label at about $6-12 per member per year to testing companies that want fewer refunds and complaints. Employers buy a capped-visit benefit.
non_obvious_insight: More testing creates a new patient, the worried well with abnormal-ish numbers, and testing companies are paid on the retest loop. An independent party paid by the patient has a credibility the vendor cannot fake. Health-anxiety CBT works, but anxious people seek doctors for reassurance, not therapists. Delivering it as a 'second opinion on your results' is the door they will walk through.
first_30_days: Contract two internists and one CBT-HA clinician part-time. Offer $99 founder-price second reads in Function and Superpower subreddits and longevity Discords. Run about 40 sessions and record pre/post anxiety scores (GAD-7 or Whiteley-7) and follow-up tests avoided. Take the outcome data to one scan center or one employer benefits broker.

title: Cool-Hours Slot Exchange for Tour Operators
one_liner: Forecast-driven heat re-scheduling for tour operators, plus a marketplace that sells 7am and 8pm venue slots, turning the coolest hours of the day into a priced, allocated resource.
customer: Independent ground-tour operators, destination management companies and cruise shore-excursion desks (10-200 guides) in Athens, Rome, Seville, Marrakech, Petra and Kyoto. The supply side is private venues (wineries, palazzi, small museums, cooking schools) with unused early and late capacity.
problem: Overtourism policy fixates on fees and caps, but the real crush is temporal: coaches, lunch and check-out times funnel everyone into 10:00-15:00, exactly when heat peaks. Operators cancel and refund ad hoc, guides carry heat-illness risk, and there is no record of duty-of-care decisions for insurers under package-travel liability. Meanwhile venues sit empty at dawn and dusk.
solution: Three layers. (1) A scheduler that ingests 5-day heat-stress (WBGT/UTCI) forecasts and the operator's tour book, rebuilds itineraries (dawn starts, indoor midday, evening loops), messages guests in their language and re-checks availability. (2) A time-stamped duty-of-care log (decisions, water and shade stops, guest health flags) exportable to insurers. (3) A slot exchange where venues list early and late timed entries at a premium and operators buy allotments in bulk. Venues get demand data to justify extended hours.
why_now: Summer 2026 Europe saw record heat and a reported provisional death toll near 38,000 (secondary source), pushing operators and regulators toward heat rules. Destinations are moving from fees to allocation: Venice's day-tripper fee reportedly did not cut numbers, while Mount Fuji's hard 4,000/day cap plus fee works. Allocation needs tooling nobody has built. Margins are squeezed by jet-fuel-driven cost increases, so avoiding refunds matters.
revenue_model: EUR 199-499 per month SaaS per operator (tiered by guide count), 4-6% take on slot-exchange GMV, and paid analytics for venues and DMOs ($10-30K per year).
non_obvious_insight: Heat converts overtourism from a space problem into a time problem, and cool hours are the unpriced scarce commodity. They can be allocated like airport slots. Operators are natural demand aggregators, so a small team can win venue supply by promising bulk purchase. The duty-of-care log is what gets insurers interested, because it cuts claim exposure.
first_30_days: Interview 20 Athens and Rome operators about summer 2026 heat-day losses. Build the scheduler as a WhatsApp plus Google Sheets workflow on open forecast data for 5 pilot operators. Get 5 private venues to commit to 08:00 or 19:30 allotments. Demo at WTM London (Nov 2026) and FITUR Madrid (Jan 2027), and convert pilots to paid before the 2027 season.

title: Zero-Return Tax Desks Inside POS Agent Shops
one_liner: Turn trusted POS agent shops into walk-in compliance desks that get informal traders their TIN and filed small-company returns before the penalties bite.
customer: Informal and micro-traders and small registered businesses (turnover under about N100m) who need to file to claim the 0% small-company rate; POS agents who earn a revenue share; principals (banks and MFBs) who want stickier merchants.
problem: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 the 0% small-company exemption (turnover about N100m or less and fixed assets under about N250m) is not automatic. You still need a TIN, records and an annual return even when tax due is zero. Filing penalties are now N100k in month one plus N50k per month after. E-invoicing reaches medium taxpayers from July 2026 and small ones from July 2027. Most shop owners are terrified of 'tax people', do not own a smartphone workflow, and cannot afford an accountant at N50-150k. Agents already see their shop's real turnover every day but never use it.
solution: A shop-counter service where the agent collects CAC, NIN and basic details on a tablet, and the platform pre-fills the TIN check and zero or small-company return using the shop's actual bank and POS statement history, with AI extraction from the pictures. A partner chartered accountant or tax practitioner reviews and signs. Recurring layer: monthly bookkeeping and a reminder feed. Later, e-invoice readiness (NRS Merchant Buyer Solution onboarding) for those crossing the next thresholds.
why_now: NTA 2025 and the Tax Administration Act took effect on 1 January 2026, with steep new late-filing penalties. The first e-invoicing go-live dates (July 2026 for medium taxpayers, July 2027 for emerging ones) are here. CBN's April 2026 single-principal rule has made agents look for non-banking revenue that keeps customers walking in. LLM extraction from photos and PDF statements is finally cheap and accurate.
revenue_model: About N7,500-15,000 per annual return, with 30-40% going to the agent. A N2,000-3,000 per month bookkeeping and reminder subscription. Referral fees from principals and accountants. Enterprise deals to give principals a white-label tax-desk feature for their agent networks.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is trust and fear, not software, and the person who has it is the agent who has known the trader for five years. Agents also hold the one thing no tax app has: 12-24 months of a shop's real transaction history. Small-company status is a 'file to be free' product, not a 'pay tax' product, so the pitch to a trader is saving a N100k fine, not helping the government.
first_30_days: Partner with one ICAN/ANAN/CITN-registered accountant who reviews and signs. Recruit 30 agents in one Lagos market cluster (for example Ikeja or Yaba) from agent WhatsApp groups. Run a 'file before the fines' campaign at N5,000 introductory price. Aim for 300 filings in 30 days, hand-checked, and document the objection patterns and the paperwork that trips people up.

title: Heir-to-Own: Sibling Buyouts on Inherited Homes
one_liner: Help the sibling who wants to keep the family house buy out the others by assuming the parent's low-rate mortgage and financing the rest.
customer: Adult heirs inheriting a home worth $300K-$1.5M where at least one wants to keep it. Distribution runs through probate attorneys and mediators. Capital comes from credit unions and community lenders.
problem: The default assumption is that inherited homes get sold and split. The recurring fight is one heir wanting to keep the house while the others want cash. The keeper often can't qualify for a cash-out refinance, because the estate isn't closed, income is thin, or no cash is on hand, so the outcome is a forced sale, a partition suit or a family break.
solution: A platform that (1) gets a neutral valuation (AVM plus appraiser) and a transparent buyout formula, (2) generates a sibling agreement covering the buyout, occupancy and carrying costs, with attorney review, and (3) structures financing: assume or continue the parent's existing low-rate first mortgage, plus a second lien or HELOC from a partner lender, closing when the estate can convey. Start as a licensed mortgage broker packaging these deals.
why_now: A large share of US mortgages carry rates near 3-4%, so the parent's loan is now valuable. Federal rules (Garn-St Germain and the CFPB successor-in-interest rules) generally let heirs keep servicing on an inherited mortgage without triggering due-on-sale. Gen X stands to inherit about $14T in the next decade (Cerulli), and market rates make cash-out refinancing unattractive.
revenue_model: Origination or broker fees of 1-1.5%, a $500-$1,500 platform fee for valuation and agreement docs, and referral or spread income from the second-lien partner.
non_obvious_insight: Locked-in low-rate mortgages turned the inherited house from an asset to liquidate into cheap capital to keep. The estate industry still defaults to 'sell', and lenders have no way to underwrite an heir with equity but no cash.
first_30_days: Pick one state. Sign five probate attorneys and one credit union. Get an MLO license or a broker partner. Handle three cases manually. Publish a free sibling-buyout calculator for estate forums and Facebook groups as the lead magnet.

title: Emerging-Market Multigrade Methods for US Microschools
one_liner: License and adapt proven low-cost, paper-based, self-paced multigrade teaching systems from Colombia, Bangladesh and India, and sell them as a turnkey kit and training to US microschools and shrinking rural districts.
customer: Microschool founders and pod networks, including the roughly 1,000 microschools the brief says are in limbo awaiting federal scholarship-credit rules, paying $1,500-5,000 a year. Homeschool co-ops with ESA money and small rural districts forced into combined-grade classes are the next buyers.
problem: One adult with 6-25 kids across several ages is now the standard microschool model. Guides are often uncredentialed (about two-thirds at Alpha School), 48% of microschool students in one dataset have special needs, and most run on screens. 61% of teachers want less device use, and AI tutors have shown no benefit over plain practice in a two-year Tennessee study.
solution: Sequenced, printable learning guides for K-6 math and literacy, peer-tutoring routines, student-run classroom governance, a 2-day guide training plus six weekly remote coaching calls, and paper mastery checkpoints. The checkpoints double as evidence for scholarship-granting organizations and ESA administrators. Licence terms give originators such as Escuela Nueva (Colombia), BRAC's one-room schools (Bangladesh) or Rishi Valley's School in a Box (India) a royalty share, so the deal funds their work too.
why_now: The federal scholarship tax credit starts in 2027 with 31 states opted in and rules still unwritten, so founders are looking for defensible academics. K-12 enrollment is heading from 49.4M to 46.9M by 2031 and more than 1,000 schools closed this year, so multi-age classes are coming to ordinary rural districts. Screen fatigue, AI bans in NYC and LAUSD, and weak AI-tutor evidence all push buyers toward paper and evidence-backed methods.
revenue_model: A one-time kit plus training at $1,500-3,000 per microschool (about $300 per student), a $600-2,400 annual coaching subscription, and district pilots at $15-40k. Royalties of 10-15% go to the licensors.
non_obvious_insight: The US treats one-adult-many-ages classrooms as a Silicon Valley invention. Countries that built them out of necessity decades ago have field-tested materials that are cheap, paper-based, robust to bad connectivity and teacher-light. Those traits match what US buyers suddenly want in 2026: fewer screens, no AI dependence, and documented outcomes. The emerging-market side is the supplier of know-how, not the customer.
first_30_days: Contact the licensors and negotiate a one-subject pilot licence (grades 2-5 math) in English. Print five paper guide sets. Recruit five microschools through founder communities and networks like the National Microschooling Center at $1,200 each. Record baseline scores with NWEA MAP or i-Ready and re-test after 10 weeks so the results become the first case study.

title: Signed-Capture Verified UGC for DTC Ads
one_liner: A capture SDK and verification API that proves a testimonial video came from a real, purchasing customer, for brands exposed to the FTC's fake-review rules.
customer: DTC and e-commerce brands spending on paid social, UGC agencies and marketplaces, and performance-marketing agencies with legal exposure.
problem: The FTC's rule on fake reviews and testimonials (effective Oct 2024) covers AI-generated testimonials from people who do not exist, with civil penalties above $50k per violation. AI 'UGC ad' generators now produce fake customers, and creators can deliver them through marketplaces without the brand knowing. Brands want real customers for conversion and cannot tell the difference.
solution: A web and native capture flow that records a testimonial with device attestation (Apple App Attest, Play Integrity), a random liveness phrase and a signed C2PA manifest, linked to a verified purchase through a Shopify order token. It outputs a 'Verified Real Customer' badge and an evidence file per ad. A batch API scans videos delivered through other tools, attests what can be attested and flags what cannot.
why_now: The FTC rule is in force, platforms are labeling AI content, and avatar-UGC volume has exploded. Provenance signals in phones and the C2PA ecosystem make signed capture cheap.
revenue_model: $3-8 per verified video, $500-3k/month agency plans, and a Shopify app subscription.
non_obvious_insight: The authenticity premium is really a compliance premium. Liability sits with the brand rather than the avatar vendor, so a legal-risk budget pays for it, not a marketing budget.
first_30_days: Ship a web capture flow linked to Shopify order tokens before any native SDK. Recruit 10 DTC brands through Shopify communities and UGC agencies at $5 per video, and run one campaign comparing verified and unverified creatives.

title: PFAS Turf Audits and Replacement Planning
one_liner: Field-by-field PFAS and regulatory risk audits plus replacement bid packages for school districts and parks departments with aging synthetic turf.
customer: School district facilities directors, athletic directors, municipal parks and recreation departments and colleges.
problem: Thousands of synthetic fields installed in the 2010s are reaching end of life just as PFAS rules bite: New York's ban on selling PFAS-containing turf takes effect December 31, 2026, California's restriction on PFAS in covered surfaces began January 1, 2026, and other states (New Jersey, Maine) have bills to pause purchases. Districts do not know what is under their fields, may not be able to buy what they always bought, and face bond votes and parent pressure.
solution: A $2.5-8k audit per district: field inventory (age, product, manufacturer), lab testing of fibers and infill through an accredited partner, legal exposure summary, lifecycle-cost comparison of synthetic, PFAS-free, hybrid and natural grass, and turnkey bid documents; then project-management and referral fees.
why_now: 2026 effective dates, active parent and environmental groups, and pending state bills create urgent, budgeted decisions.
revenue_model: $2.5-8k audits, testing pass-through margin, 2-4 percent project-management fees on $500k-1.5M projects, supplier referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: Nobody owns 'what is my turf made of' data and manufacturers will not volunteer it. Sitting between district, lab and contractor makes you the neutral spec writer who controls the RFP.
first_30_days: Build a public-records inventory of turf fields in New York from bond documents and board minutes, pitch 50 districts, line up an accredited lab, and sell three audits.

title: Pattern-Less Foundry Network via Printed Sand Molds
one_liner: Print sand molds centrally and pour them at idle small foundries to deliver castings in about two weeks with no patterns.
customer: Pump, valve, ag-equipment and machinery OEMs and repair shops needing 5-500 castings. Small foundries are the supply side.
problem: Small-lot castings from Asia now face tariffs and freight up to 50% higher. Domestic foundries quote long lead times, largely because of pattern-making and minimum runs, and aging owners are retiring or closing. Castings are an invisible bottleneck under reshoring and under Section 232 derivative rates.
solution: A hub with binder-jet sand printing (or rented capacity at existing bureaus) prints mold and core packages from customer CAD plus solidification simulation. Ship them to 10-30 small foundries that pour iron, steel or aluminum. The network handles NDT, dimensional checks and certs, including melt origin. Start with one or two alloys and repair and replacement parts.
why_now: Printed sand has improved in cost and speed, tariffs and freight punish imported castings, foundries are consolidating, and simulation and AI gating design are cheap.
revenue_model: Per-casting pricing with 25-35% gross margin. $500-3k engineering fee per part. Foundries pay for mold volume routed to them.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is patterns and scheduling, not melting. Many small foundries have idle furnace hours but no digital front door, and a printed mold is a universal interface. US-melt certification is a sales kicker, not the core.
first_30_days: Sign three foundries with idle capacity. Buy printed molds from an existing bureau. Take 10 orders for obsolete pump or gearbox housings at $1-3k each, using 3D scans of broken parts.

title: FTC Review-Rule Audits for Franchisors
one_liner: Fixed-fee audits that find review gating, incentivised reviews and insider reviews across a franchisor's or dealer group's locations, and in the reputation vendors doing it for them.
customer: General counsel and marketing VPs at franchisors and multi-location operators (auto dealer groups, dental support organisations, home-services and fitness franchises), with reputation-management agencies as channel partners.
problem: The FTC Consumer Review Rule bans review gating, sentiment-conditional incentives, suppression and undisclosed insider reviews, with civil penalties of up to $53,088 per violation. The FTC sent 10 warning letters in Dec 2025 and obtained a $4M order (partly suspended) in July 2026. Local operators often use review-request software that quietly routes unhappy customers away from public sites, and franchisors are exposed to franchisee behaviour.
solution: A 'Rule Ready' audit. Scan Google, Yelp, Facebook and vertical sites across all locations for suspicious bursts, employee reviews and incentive language. Mystery-shop vendors' review-request flows (does a 2-star responder get diverted from Google?). Deliver a risk-ranked location report and remediation playbook, then quarterly monitoring and a vendor certification for compliant review-request software.
why_now: Warning letters (Dec 2025), the first orders (July 2026) and law-firm commentary in mid-2026 show an enforcement pattern taking shape, and Italy's Mar 2026 Trustpilot fine shows the referee itself can be penalised.
revenue_model: $5-25k per audit scaled by location count, $2-8k per month monitoring, and certification fees from review-software vendors.
non_obvious_insight: Liability sits with the buyer of reputation software, not the vendor, and those vendors' flows were designed when gating was legal. The money follows the risk to the franchisor's general counsel.
first_30_days: Pick one vertical, either dental support organisations or auto dealer groups. Cold-email 40 general counsel with a free three-location sample audit. Build scanners on public review data and line up two law firms as referral partners.

title: Human Bench Network for AI Agents
one_liner: An API-fronted network of laid-off expert bench scientists who run ad hoc wet-lab experiments for AI agents and return machine-readable execution records.
customer: AI-first biotechs, AI-for-science startups and university groups (5-60 people, seed to Series B) that run agent swarms but have no wet lab; later, programs adjacent to frontier labs.
problem: Agent swarms now propose far more experiments than anyone can run. Anthropic's run went from 200,000+ reverse transcriptases to 20 candidates using ~950 agents in 21 hours. Stanford's Virtual Biotech (37,000 agents, Science, Sept 17, 2026) says the next step is testing findings in real labs. Cloud labs and robots handle fixed assays, but not ad hoc molecular biology: Anthropic itself found robotics less conducive to ad hoc workflows and kept human scientists at the bench. Human review and bench work are the bottleneck.
solution: Ticketed experiments through an API or MCP endpoint. The agent proposes a protocol and a senior scientist does feasibility triage. A vetted contractor then runs it at sublet or surplus benches, BSL-1/2 only. Each job returns a signed record that separates AI proposal, human edit and physical execution (deviations, photos, instrument logs, raw data). Fixed price per experiment. Start with commodity molecular biology: cloning, small-scale expression and purification, ELISA/BLI/qPCR, enzyme activity, bacterial and cell-culture assays.
why_now: Frontier labs and Stanford now say publicly that bench execution is the bottleneck. BioSpace tracks 15,000+ biopharma job cuts across 50+ companies in 2026, which supplies skilled hands. The OpenAI Foundation plans to distribute $1B by year-end through Public Data for Health, which creates grant-funded demand for data generation. Lab Manager notes there is no sign-off standard for AI-directed experiments, and this record format supplies one. Anthropic has said it wants to work with other scientists.
revenue_model: $1.5-8k per experiment at roughly 35-45% gross margin, monthly retainers with minimum volumes for agent-heavy customers, and a premium for 48-hour turnaround. The platform keeps a take rate on contractor labor.
non_obvious_insight: Compute is now nearly free compared with bench throughput, and robots failed as the universal answer because real biology is ad hoc. The defensible assets are a pre-vetted pool of humans and a structured execution record that agents can learn from. Humans become the last-mile actuator for AI. Adaptyv and cloud labs cover single fixed assays; nobody sells the long tail of one-off experiments.
first_30_days: Recruit 10-15 laid-off molecular biologists in Boston, SF and San Diego through layoff trackers and alumni groups. Rent 2-3 sublet benches or surplus CRO benches. Define three ticket types with fixed prices. Pitch 10 AI protein-design and agent startups and close 3-5 pilots. Aim for the first 20 paid experiments and publish the sample record schema.

title: Savings-Group Credit Score and Treasury
one_liner: Turn informal savings groups into a credit bureau and stablecoin treasury that asset financiers can lend against.
customer: Financiers of productive assets (solar irrigation, motorbikes, milk coolers) and NGOs, with savings groups as end users.
problem: Sandi AI already reaches 10,000+ farmer groups that buy solar irrigation from pooled savings rather than loans. Chamas, VSLAs, tandas and arisan have no records that lenders can see.
solution: A WhatsApp and USSD ledger that logs contributions and minutes, produces a group credit history and optionally holds a stablecoin group treasury that diaspora members can top up. The wedge is selling qualified-group leads to asset financiers.
why_now: Kenya and Nigeria are legitimising stablecoins, local-language voice models can log minutes, and Sandi AI has shown demand.
revenue_model: $20-60 per funded asset lead, plus a 0.5% treasury fee.
non_obvious_insight: The group is the unit of trust in informal finance. Digitising it creates a bureau that cannot be scraped from mobile money data.
first_30_days: Sign 100 groups in Kenya through one NGO and record three months of contributions to prove predictive value.

title: Night Season: After-Dark Programming for Heat-Struck Venues
one_liner: A turnkey production company that converts heat-crushed summer attendance at zoos, gardens and ballparks into ticketed after-dark shows, with heat-triggered scheduling, on revenue share.
customer: Zoos, botanical gardens, minor-league ballparks, county fairs and water parks in the Sun Belt and Southwest, whose summer midday attendance collapses in heat waves and who set 2027 programming budgets in Q4.
problem: Extreme heat kills midday visits and creates heat-illness liability, while venue infrastructure sits idle. Venues know night events work (winter light shows, adult zoo nights) but lack lantern, projection or lighting capex, production talent and a heat protocol. New heat rules for outdoor workers in California, Washington and Oregon, with a federal OSHA rule targeted for October 2027, also make midday staffing costlier.
solution: A 'Night Season' program run from June to September. Lantern trails, projection mapping, night-safari tours, film and music nights, with hours moved by a WBGT trigger and a documented heat-safety protocol. We supply the show kit (leased), lighting crew, ticketing setup and sponsors such as hospitals and utilities as 'heat-safe' partners. The venue supplies land and staff.
why_now: Summer 2026 was reported as the hottest US July on record, so 2027 budgets will assume it repeats. LED lantern and projection costs have fallen, and WBGT sensors are cheap. Entertainment production talent is underemployed after studio and game cuts. Venues want revenue that does not depend on midday gates.
revenue_model: 35-45% of ticket and F&B revenue with no fee to the venue, leased show kits, and sponsorships. Illustrative math: 40 nights x 1,000 guests x $22 is about $880K gross per venue-season.
non_obvious_insight: Heat does not kill demand for outdoor leisure. It moves it about eight hours later. What blocks venues is show capex and know-how. A documented WBGT-triggered schedule shift is also a heat-illness risk reduction that a venue's liability insurer may recognize, so the program can help offset its own cost.
first_30_days: Pitch 10 Sun Belt zoos and gardens during the Q4 planning window with a mock-up and a $99 founders-pass landing page at two venues to test pre-sales. Sign a lantern or projection vendor on revenue share. Run a small heat-shifted pilot weekend in Arizona this October, while evenings are warm.

title: Federal-Equipment Disposition Desk for Closing Labs
one_liner: A compliance-plus-resale service that clears federal-interest, decontaminates and re-homes grant-funded instruments when labs shrink or close.
customer: University research-administration and property offices, independent research institutes, SBIR-funded startups winding down, and the roughly 300 'zombie' biotechs Owl Posting counts.
problem: Instruments bought with federal funds carry federal-interest and disposition rules (2 CFR 200.313, with a per-unit threshold), which stall resale. Freezers, cryostats and sequencers sit idle or get trashed. NIH grant terminations, 15,000+ biopharma job cuts and 50+ shrinking companies add supply, while small labs cannot afford new equipment. The brief flags used-equipment liquidation for squeezed labs as an underserved gap.
solution: An asset-level 'federal-interest passport': identify the award and agency, determine the obligation, prepare disposition requests and valuation, arrange decontamination certificates, pack and ship, and list to vetted buyers. Commission plus compliance fee.
why_now: Funding turbulence and layoffs are producing lab closures now, and marketplaces for used equipment exist but do not solve permission or liability.
revenue_model: 15-25% commission on resale, $500-2,500 per-asset compliance fees, and institutional annual retainers.
non_obvious_insight: The seller's pain is permission and liability, not price discovery, so marketplaces do not fix it. The compliance passport is the unlock, and attaching one at purchase time makes instruments 'resale-ready' and turns the desk into a recurring service.
first_30_days: Contact 10 mid-tier university property or research-admin offices and 30 winding-down SBIR startups. Process 5 pilot disposals. Template the passport. Partner with a decontamination and shipping vendor.

title: Supplier-side questionnaire firewall citing the VSME cap
one_liner: A forward-to tool that answers big customers' ESG, NIS2 and EUDR questionnaires from one evidence vault and flags which questions the law says a small supplier can decline.
customer: EU SMEs and small mid-caps (under 1,000 staff) that supply larger companies, bought through accountants, tax advisors and chambers of commerce who add it as a service to their clients.
problem: Since Omnibus I took effect on 18 March 2026, CSRD-scope buyers cannot require value-chain partners with 1,000 or fewer employees to provide more sustainability information than the voluntary SME standard (VSME) sets out. The VSME basic module covers business description, workforce, energy and Scope 1 and 2 emissions. The cap does not cover NIS2 security questionnaires, EUDR data, voluntary customer targets or bid competition. Suppliers still get differently formatted questionnaires from every customer and lender, and most cannot tell which asks are legally capped.
solution: Suppliers forward each customer questionnaire (Excel, PDF or portal export) to an inbox. The tool parses it and maps each question to a canonical evidence vault: VSME basic answers, energy and payroll-derived Scope 1 and 2 numbers, a NIS2-lite control evidence set, and a supplier code of conduct. It auto-drafts answers. It also classifies every question as 'inside the cap', 'outside the cap, with a cited polite decline paragraph', or 'not covered by the cap (NIS2, EUDR, voluntary)'. The vault is built by pulling data the accountant already holds. Accountants get a multi-client dashboard.
why_now: The cap is 6 months old and the VSME Delegated Act was published in July 2026, so customers' procurement teams are still sending old-format questionnaires. Germany's NIS2 law took effect on 6 Dec 2025 and BSI says regulated entities will grow from about 4,500 to about 29,500, which multiplies supplier security questionnaires. CSDDD also limits information requests to smaller firms, but application is not until 2029.
revenue_model: White-label to accountancies at EUR 15-30 per client per month, or direct at EUR 49-99 per month per SME. Add EUR 150-300 for a one-off 'initial vault build' for firms not served by an accountant.
non_obvious_insight: The crowded market sells to large buyers who send questionnaires. The legally new wedge is the supplier's right to refuse, plus the accountant, who already holds energy and payroll data and is trusted. Evidence: after 18 March 2026 large CSRD companies 'cannot require value-chain partners with 1,000 or fewer employees to provide more sustainability information than ... VSME', but the same source warns that 'Nothing stops a buyer choosing the bidder who turned up with clean, current numbers' and that Scope 1 and 2 are non-negotiable, so suppliers need both a decline lever and a ready pack (https://www.dashe.ai/blog/big-customer-asked-for-your-emissions/). Suppliers to NIS2 entities 'should expect questionnaires' and sending a 300-question form is common (https://www.3rdrisk.com/blog/seven-nis2-questions-to-ask). Germany's NIS2 registration had only 38.5% compliance by the March 2026 deadline (https://www.cloudmagazin.com/en/2026/03/22/nis2-and-saas-supply-chain-compliance-gap/).
first_30_days: Collect 30 real questionnaires by offering accountants a free 'questionnaire triage' in exchange for the redacted files. Hand-map them to a 60-row canonical answer sheet. Build the classify-and-decline prototype on that set. Pitch 5 small accounting firms and 2 chamber-of-commerce sustainability desks with a live demo on a client's own questionnaire. Aim for 3 paying accountancy pilots.

title: Fresh-Address Desk for Medicaid Plans
one_liner: Turn Title I front offices into a consent-based channel that keeps families on Medicaid, paid per household retained by health plans and hospitals, with a revenue share to the school.
customer: Medicaid managed care plans (member retention and quality-bonus teams) and nonprofit hospitals with community-benefit budgets. Principals and PTAs are the channel partners and receive a revenue share. They do not pay.
problem: Six-month renewals and work-requirement paperwork are scheduled to hit expansion-adult Medicaid enrollees in 2027. Plans lose members when renewal mail goes to old addresses and phone numbers, and their call-center contact rates are dismal. Kids often lose coverage in the household churn even when they stay eligible. Plans cannot reach the families who most need help, and the parent hears the plan's mail as junk.
solution: A text-first, home-language 'update your info and check your renewal' flow built into the school's existing August packet and registration. A part-time parent-liaison 'benefits desk' sits in the front office a few hours a week. Data goes to a plan only with a signed opt-in parent consent, not under FERPA directory information. Plans pay a fee per verified address or phone update and per completed renewal. About 30 percent of the revenue goes to a school-controlled discretionary fund. The same desk later handles other bounty-paying programs: utility low-income enrollment, Lifeline phone and internet plans, Summer EBT, and vision and dental follow-up.
why_now: Under the 2025 budget reconciliation law, expansion-adult redeterminations move to every 6 months after the end of 2026 and work requirements begin in 2027, unless states get a delay. The post-COVID Medicaid unwinding showed that most coverage losses were procedural. Principals are also hungry for discretionary dollars after the 2025 federal freezes and cancelled school-mental-health grants.
revenue_model: Per-household bounty of roughly $25 to $75 for a verified update or completed renewal. Plans also pay an annual per-school or per-region program fee. Optional add-on bounties from utilities and phone carriers.
non_obvious_insight: The freshest address and phone database of low-income families is not held by any agency. It is held by the school secretary, who re-verifies it every August because busing, lunch and emergency cards depend on it. Families ignore the plan's letters but answer the office they trust. Principals will only say yes if the money flows back to the school and consent is explicit, and that design is the moat.
first_30_days: Pick one state and call the community-engagement or quality director at two or three Medicaid plans. Offer a 90-day pilot in 3 schools whose principals you already know, priced per verified update. Build it with Twilio and a bilingual part-timer, and use a hashed list-match to show how many of a plan's returned-mail members appear in school records. Have the principal co-sign a one-page consent form that PTA volunteers can hand out.
